text:
alex-procurement: FYI vendor (SeaSwift) just flagged AWB 645-188-CH as damaged in transit and opened a claim. They recommend redirecting the replacement batch to FRA depot instead of AMS to avoid a customs reclass. Can we decide?

maria-sre: How many units impacted and which SKUs? Need to check cluster reserve.

jordan-ops: It's 8x H100s (sku H100-GEN2-80). If FRA becomes the handoff, ETA +48h vs +72h to AMS. FRA avoids extra HS paperwork per vendor.

alex-procurement: Vendor says immediate air uplift option available for extra cost (~$14k) to meet the original SLA window. Sea expedite (rebook on next feeder) would likely push +5 days.

hannah-finance: Hold — can we get line-item for expedited air? Also what about insurance payout timeline vs vendor credit?

tao-logistics: @hannah-finance I pulled the manifest. Claim ref SW-CLAIM-2026-438. Carrier notes physical damage on pallet 3. Insurance estimate pending but vendor can ship replacements from nearby pool in FRA today if we accept air uplift charge. Link to manifest: https://files.supplierswift.com/manifest/SW-645-188-CH

lina-pm: Heads up — if we lose those 8 H100s for 5 days, the eu-inference-prod pool latency SLO for the nightly batch job may hit 250ms for a short window. We have one canary rollout scheduled tomorrow night. Need mitigation plan.

maria-sre: Mitigation options: 1) borrow 4 units from reserved warm pool in APAC (cross-region penalty), 2) enable temporary autoscale to Dedicated spare (will increase spend), 3) delay canary. Which do we prefer?

jordan-ops: Quick calc: cross-region borrow adds ~30% per-token cost, autoscale to Dedicated adds flat $9k/day. Air uplift is $14k one-time. If SLA hit is unacceptable, air uplift seems cheapest relative to SLO penalty + customer impact.

hannah-finance: Can approve up to $12k without exec signoff. Need an extra $2k sign-off from leads or procurement head.

alex-procurement: @maria-sre @lina-pm decision request: Approve air uplift to FRA now (cost $14k) OR accept 5-day sea delay and use temporary autoscale for canary? We're leaning to uplift but need signoff for the $2k delta.

maria-sre: Approve. Cluster impact outweighs the delta — we need canary to proceed.

lina-pm: Approve as well. Canary is higher priority for next-week launch.

tao-logistics: Noted. I'll confirm with SeaSwift and ask for expedited invoice and AWB for tracking. ETA to FRA customs clearance will be ~24h after uplfit departure. I'll post AWB once generated.

deploy-bot: [deploy-scheduler] Canary rollout for eu-inference-prod paused pending resource confirmation.

jordan-ops: After Tao posts AWB, ops will tag the shipment to the FRA crossdock queue and reserve dock window 14:00-18:00 CET. Also need depot acceptance email before arrival to avoid return.

hannah-finance: I'll pre-approve the $2k exception; send invoice to finance@redwood.example and CC me. We'll expedite payment after receiving vendor invoice and manifest.

alex-procurement: Thanks all. @tao-logistics please escalate insurance claim SW-CLAIM-2026-438 concurrently; we need proof of damage for vendor credit path in case uplift doesn't go through.

tao-logistics: Will do. Uploading photos and POD to the claim portal now. Reference: https://claims.seaswift.example/SW-CLAIM-2026-438

maria-sre: Ops/SRE to monitor eu-inference-prod latency window tonight. I'll post a short runbook: if p95 > 220ms for >15m, rollback canary and we trigger autoscale.

lina-pm: I'll update stakeholders and pause non-critical canaries in the EU until confirmed delivered.

alex-procurement: I'll update the procurement tracker and mark vendor as expedited. Filing this under PO-9931 replacement flow.

jordan-ops: One more ask — can vendor include serials for replacements in AWB so we can pre-seed inventory? saves time on depot acceptance.

tao-logistics: Asked them to include serials; vendor says "yes" if uplift chosen. Will share AWB + serial list in thread once available.

alex-procurement: Great. Closing loop once AWB arrives. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
